ladder.header: Historical maximum progress in any attempt; final state and task success are separate judgments.

levels.text:
Initial state before the first verified milestone.
The episode begins; record S0 when no later milestone is supported.

The gripper is aligned to capture the marker.
The jaws visibly bracket a graspable marker segment with an approach direction and opening that could trap it.
Distant approach, merely reaching the workspace, or a jaw close with visibly wrong geometry does not establish alignment.
Alignment remains achieved if a later close misses.

The gripper establishes a secure hold of the marker.
The same marker segment is visibly captured and retained between the jaws across multiple consecutive frames.
Use jaw-object geometry or coherent small motion to establish retention; the marker may still be supported by the table.
Jaw closure alone, a brief pinch, brushing, or immediate slip does not establish a secure grasp.
Lifting and insertion-compatible tip protrusion are not required for this stage; a secure but badly positioned grasp can still fail later.

The gripper lifts the retained marker clear of the table.
The marker visibly clears table support under sustained gripper control.
Dragging, pivoting on the table, or a one-frame bounce is insufficient.
Travel away from the grasp site is not required.

The held marker is upright and aligned over a specific holder hole.
The retained marker is at the holder and oriented approximately vertically along the hole's insertion axis.
The lower tip is positioned over the intended hole opening; verify local geometry primarily in WRIST.
Making the marker vertical elsewhere is insufficient.
SIDE-view overlap, exterior contact, or a downward push beside the holder does not prove alignment.
No pause before entry is required.

The marker tip engages and begins entering a holder hole.
The tip visibly descends into the intended opening and the holder occludes the entered portion.
An insertion-directed motion or contact with the top rim alone is not hole engagement.
SIDE holder contact and pushing down onto the table beside the holder are not engagement.
Full seating and release are not required; a later jam or partial release does not erase this stage.

The fully seated marker is released and retained by the holder.
Full insertion depth is positively verified before release.
The jaws open and relinquish the marker; the holder retains it fully seated and upright.
The gripper moves clear, or recording ends after the jaws are visibly no longer clamping the marker while it stays seated.
A partial insertion that is released does not establish S6.
Jaw opening while still clamping, a held fully seated marker, or an ambiguous final frame is insufficient.
Do not invent gripper clearance when recording cuts off.

task_definition.objective: Align for a marker grasp, establish a secure hold, lift clear of the table, orient the marker vertically over a holder hole, engage the hole, and release the fully seated marker. Track achieved milestones separately from the failure cause and final physical state.
successCriteria: The marker has visibly entered a holder hole and reached full seating depth.
The jaws visibly release the fully seated marker and the holder retains it upright.
The gripper moves clear, or recording cuts off only after the jaws visibly stop clamping the fully seated marker; do not infer release from intent or a supplied outcome.
Success is judged at the endpoint; later loss of an earlier seated-and-released state is a failure without erasing the achieved milestone.

entities.description: Whiteboard marker manipulated by the robot.
Red/orange movable block containing insertion holes.

evidenceViews.description: Third-person side_1 view for global motion, table support, marker location, and holder motion.
caveats: Perspective can make separated geometry overlap.
SIDE overlap alone never proves holder arrival, contact, or insertion.

evidenceViews.description: wrist_left view; primary for local gripper/marker/holder/hole geometry when usable.
caveats: May point away or be occluded.
If usable during transport but the holder never appears, holder alignment and engagement are not supported; the highest supported milestone is at most S3.

stages.name: Start
stages.description: Initial state before the first verified milestone.
entryCriteria: The episode begins; record S0 when no later milestone is supported.

stages.name: Align for grasp
stages.description: The gripper is aligned to capture the marker.
entryCriteria: The jaws visibly bracket a graspable marker segment with an approach direction and opening that could trap it.
exclusions: Distant approach, merely reaching the workspace, or a jaw close with visibly wrong geometry does not establish alignment.
Alignment remains achieved if a later close misses.

stages.name: Grasp the marker
stages.description: The gripper establishes a secure hold of the marker.
entryCriteria: The same marker segment is visibly captured and retained between the jaws across multiple consecutive frames.
Use jaw-object geometry or coherent small motion to establish retention; the marker may still be supported by the table.
exclusions: Jaw closure alone, a brief pinch, brushing, or immediate slip does not establish a secure grasp.
Lifting and insertion-compatible tip protrusion are not required for this stage; a secure but badly positioned grasp can still fail later.

stages.name: Lift the marker
stages.description: The gripper lifts the retained marker clear of the table.
entryCriteria: The marker visibly clears table support under sustained gripper control.
exclusions: Dragging, pivoting on the table, or a one-frame bounce is insufficient.
Travel away from the grasp site is not required.

stages.name: Align the marker for insertion
stages.description: The held marker is upright and aligned over a specific holder hole.
entryCriteria: The retained marker is at the holder and oriented approximately vertically along the hole's insertion axis.
The lower tip is positioned over the intended hole opening; verify local geometry primarily in WRIST.
exclusions: Making the marker vertical elsewhere is insufficient.
SIDE-view overlap, exterior contact, or a downward push beside the holder does not prove alignment.
No pause before entry is required.

stages.name: Engage the holder hole
stages.description: The marker tip engages and begins entering a holder hole.
entryCriteria: The tip visibly descends into the intended opening and the holder occludes the entered portion.
exclusions: An insertion-directed motion or contact with the top rim alone is not hole engagement.
SIDE holder contact and pushing down onto the table beside the holder are not engagement.
Full seating and release are not required; a later jam or partial release does not erase this stage.

stages.name: Release the fully seated marker
stages.description: The fully seated marker is released and retained by the holder.
entryCriteria: Full insertion depth is positively verified before release.
The jaws open and relinquish the marker; the holder retains it fully seated and upright.
The gripper moves clear, or recording ends after the jaws are visibly no longer clamping the marker while it stays seated.
exclusions: A partial insertion that is released does not establish S6.
Jaw opening while still clamping, a held fully seated marker, or an ambiguous final frame is insufficient.
Do not invent gripper clearance when recording cuts off.

keyActions.name: Approach marker workspace
keyActions.description: The gripper enters a pose from which marker interaction is plausible.
keyActions.stageRelation: Approach is an independent action and does not by itself establish S1 alignment.

keyActions.name: Align for grasp
keyActions.description: The jaws and approach direction become arranged so closing could trap the marker.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S1 alignment; may share its time with a grasp when both are visible.

keyActions.name: Attempt grasp
keyActions.description: The jaws execute a committed close/contact attempt on the marker.
keyActions.stageRelation: A close attempt supports but does not prove S2 secure grasp.

keyActions.name: Securely grasp marker
keyActions.description: The gripper establishes a secure hold of the marker. Establish retention across consecutive frames independently of table clearance.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S2 grasp; a close attempt and a lift remain separate actions.

keyActions.name: Securely lift marker
keyActions.description: The marker is retained across frames and lifted clear of the table.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S3 lift; travel away is not required.

keyActions.name: Transport retained marker
keyActions.description: The retained marker moves away from the grasp site with the gripper.
keyActions.stageRelation: Transport may follow S3 and supports arrival for S4; it is not a separate human stage.

keyActions.name: Arrive at holder
keyActions.description: Local geometry establishes that the retained marker reaches the holder area.
keyActions.stageRelation: Necessary for S4 local alignment, but arrival alone does not prove orientation or hole alignment.

keyActions.name: Align marker tip with hole
keyActions.description: The marker tip is visibly positioned over a specific hole opening.
keyActions.stageRelation: Necessary for S4 together with an upright, insertion-compatible marker orientation.

keyActions.name: Contact holder
keyActions.description: The retained marker visibly contacts any holder surface.
keyActions.stageRelation: Contact can occur without entry. Only positive hole engagement establishes S5.

keyActions.name: Enter holder hole
keyActions.description: The marker tip visibly enters a specific holder hole.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required for S5 hole engagement and S6 successful release.

keyActions.name: Reach full insertion depth
keyActions.description: Visible geometry positively establishes full seating.
keyActions.stageRelation: Required before S6 release; full depth while held is recorded as an action within S5.

keyActions.name: Open gripper jaws
keyActions.description: The gripper jaws visibly open or visibly begin to part from the marker. Report the first frame where the finger gap visibly grows, never an earlier frame of intent.
keyActions.stageRelation: Necessary but not sufficient for S6: the marker must be fully seated and actually relinquished.

keyActions.name: Move gripper clear
keyActions.description: The gripper retreats enough to test independent holder retention.
keyActions.stageRelation: Confirms independent retention after S6 release; omit when recording ends before retreat.

failureModes.description: No terminal failure; use only for verified successful release with a retained fully seated endpoint.
No useful approach into the marker workspace.
Approach geometry prevents a viable grasp.
Yaw misalignment prevents a viable grasp.
The gripper approaches but never executes a committed close.
A committed close after alignment fails to establish secure marker retention; do not use merely because a secure grasp fails to lift.
The grasp is unusable for insertion because the marker tip does not protrude.
The gripper pinches an end without establishing a secure insertion-usable grasp.
A retained marker gradually escapes before holder interaction.
A retained marker drops during transport for a reason other than gradual slip.
The retained marker reaches useful transport but has an insertion-incompatible orientation.
A visible grasp-angle error is not corrected before holder interaction.
The retained marker contacts the holder and then retreats without insertion.
The retained marker reaches the holder vicinity but misses it without visible contact.
The marker visibly enters partially and then jams.
A partial insertion is released and retained but never fully seated.
The marker remains held at video end and no more specific visible causal failure applies.
The retained marker touches the TOP holder face or top rim/edge without entering a hole.
The insertion occurs at a false location: SIDE holder contact or a downward push onto the TABLE beside the holder.
The marker partially enters a holder hole other than the visible task target.
The jaws release at the holder and the marker ends unretained without retained partial insertion.
The marker reaches holder contact or shallow entry, then slips or is pulled out before retained release.
A directly visible failure not covered by a more specific declared mode.

finalStates.description: The marker rests on the table.
The gripper retains the marker away from the holder.
The gripper retains the marker at the holder.
The marker is partially inserted and still held.
The holder retains a released partial insertion.
The marker is fully seated and still held.
The holder retains a released fully seated marker.
At the final visible frame the marker is fully seated in a holder hole, the jaws have visibly begun to open and are no longer clamping it, and the recording ends before the gripper moves clear.
The marker has dropped out of the supported workspace.
The final marker state cannot be determined.

decisionRules.rule: Each numbered stage is a positively achieved milestone, not an attempt or failure category. Timestamp the first evidence that its criteria are met. A failed episode whose maximum is S{k} for k < 6 is summarized as 'reached S{k}; failed to reach S{k+1}'. Do not assign S{k+1} merely because it was attempted. Keep the concrete causal failure enum separate from this progress summary.

Compute max_stage as the highest positively achieved stage across all attempts, not the final physical state. A later slip, drop, or loss of seating does not erase earlier progress. A failure after S6 means the completed result was later lost, not failure to reach a nonexistent S7. A recovered failure event does not by itself make the final outcome a failure.

Grasp and lift, or alignment and engagement, may share a timestamp if independently supported in that frame. Do not invent intermediate times or achievements to fill the ladder. Occlusion means not verified, not proof the milestone never happened: use the lower supported maximum, flag human review, and explain uncertain boundaries.

If a human_outcome_anchor is supplied, retain it as authoritative binary outcome context, not as evidence of a stage or timestamp. Never invent alignment, grasp, lift, entry, release, or seating to satisfy it. If the visible milestones or endpoint cannot support its terminal semantics, flag the conflict for human review; do not hide it with coerced stage labels.

S2 is secure retention even on the table. S3 additionally requires clear table clearance under gripper control. A miss remains at the highest earlier verified milestone; a sustained grasp followed by a failed lift reaches S2.

Use SIDE for global motion and WRIST for local geometry. If usable WRIST never shows the holder, do not award S4 or S5 from SIDE overlap. A genuinely unusable view warrants uncertainty, not invented geometry.
S4 requires both upright insertion-compatible orientation and the retained marker tip over a specific holder hole. Vertical orientation elsewhere is not enough.

TOP holder face/rim contact without entry maps to holder_contact_no_insertion. SIDE holder contact or a downward push onto the TABLE beside the holder maps to false_insertion. Neither establishes S5. Preserve any earlier genuine alignment.

S5 requires positive tip entry into a specific holder hole. A partial entry followed by a jam or release still achieves S5; partial-release and fully-seated-held states are endpoint/action distinctions, not extra stages.

S6 requires visible full-depth seating followed by actual loss of jaw retention while the holder supports the marker. Timestamp the first frame where release and full seated retention are verified. A fully seated marker still clamped is S5, not S6.

Preserve the existing narrow cutoff allowance: S6 may be verified before gripper clearance only if multiple terminal frames establish full seating, visible jaw parting that stops clamping, and stable upright holder retention. Use marker_release_committed_at_cutoff, report move_gripper_clear as absent, and never substitute opening intent for actual relinquishment.

Audit the final WRIST sequence, not one frame. If full depth or loss of clamping cannot be verified, keep the lower supported stage and request review. Do not promote the stage solely to match a supplied human outcome.

auditProcedure: Locate the marker, gripper, holder, and relevant hole in synchronized SIDE and WRIST evidence.
Segment chronological attempts and preserve achieved progress across later slips or retries.
Independently verify alignment, secure grasp, clear lift, local vertical insertion alignment, hole engagement, and fully seated release.
Record every declared key action independently, including full seating while held and unsuccessful jaw openings; do not expose these as additional human stages.
Inspect the final second for actual release and retained full seating; use the narrowly defined cutoff state only when all evidence gates hold.
Choose the physical final state and causal failure enum separately from the highest stage. For a failed episode below S6, name the next unreached milestone; request review for unobserved boundaries.
Cross-check stage/action identities, transition times, failure onset, endpoint, success, and any human-outcome conflict.
